title: Base-change, proper-refinement and identity equations for the graph map
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. For the specific core canonicalEtaleCompactSupportCore defined in [lem-asd-compact-support-graph-derived-isomorphism], the proposition EtaleCompactSupportCoherence [def-asd-compact-support-graph-comparison] holds. Thus its comparison $a^{-1}$ intertwines the specified compact-support and sum exchanges for every change of locally Noetherian quasi-compact base; for every proper refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] its comparisons obey the exact direct-image-composition equation of that proposition; and for the proper identity compactification it equals identityEtaleCompactSupportComparison. These are equations of actual unbounded derived transformations. No adjoint-uniqueness or double-base-change clause is assumed.

proof.text: Use the already proved graph-comparison identification and arbitrary-base exact exchange equation from GraphExchange in EtaleCompactSupportGraphGeometricBaseChange. Replace its forward comparison by compactSupportDerivedComparison. Cancel its invertible pullback and the inverse graph comparison on the base-changed compactification to obtain the base_change equation for canonicalEtaleCompactSupportCore.

Reuse the proved open_compare_mono from UnboundedProperOpenComposition, which embeds open extension by zero into ordinary direct image. Direct image and its composition isomorphism preserve this monomorphism. A generic calculation for two successive right-adjoint transports identifies the transpose of a section of an invertible counit with extension of its inverse. Applied to the existing lowerStarUnit_comp_counit equation, this gives graph normalization for an open immersion directly into the open comparison map. For a refinement r:c→d, compose the two sheaf graph maps followed by lowerStarComp(r,d.g). After postcomposing with the monic compactification-to-direct-image map for c, naturality and associativity of lowerStarComp reduce the composite to graph normalization for r and then for d. Thus it equals the graph map for c. No duplicate downstream comparison lemmas are declared or relocated.

Use the shared normalizationHomotopyComponent formula for the normalized graph component on a homotopy representative as the exact source factorization, Qh of the sheaf map, Qh of the inverse homotopy composition comparison, the right-derived unit, and the image of the inverse exact open-extension factorization. Its five-factor formula matches compactSupportComparisonOnHomotopy and the existing component theorem identifies compactSupportDerivedComparison on Qh with it. In the generic coherence calculations, the homotopy composition comparison for a literal composite simplifies to identity. In the composite of two such components, cancel the intermediate exact factors. Move the first derived unit past the second sheaf map by naturality and move the final exact factor past the derived direct-image compositor. The compositor factorization comp_fac and comp_unit_app identify the remaining two units with the unit of the composite. The sheaf refinement equation from step 2 then proves the forward derived refinement equation. Localization full faithfulness extends it from every homotopy representative to all derived objects; cancellation of the invertible graph comparisons gives the required refinement equation.

For the proper identity compactification, postcompose the graph map with the monic inclusion into direct image. Graph normalization, equality of etale and open comparison maps, the right unit law for lowerStarComp, and naturality of lowerStarId show that this graph map is the inverse lowerStarId whiskered by extension by zero. For its derived normalization, move the exact-derived direct-image comparison past the inverse exact factor and use rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac. Move the derived lowerStarId and identity comparisons past the same factor. mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fach and the existing mapDerivedCategoryIdIso_hom_app_Qh_obj equation identify their normalized composite with Qh of lowerStarId. The homotopy identity cancellation is proved on a complex representative degree by degree, without unfolding the derived functors. The latter cancels Qh of its inverse in the graph map, leaving the exact factor and its inverse. Localization extends this identity to all derived objects. Cancel the forward graph comparison to conclude equality of the two specified identity isomorphisms.
